events.feedback:
Here is a critical, fact-first review of the Texas Olive (Cordia boissieri) draft.

The tone is excellent—direct, grounded, and does a great job explaining the botanical relationship to the Geiger tree without over-hyping it.

🔍 Fact-Check & Technical Precision
The "Non-Native / Not Invasive" Badges: This is 100% correct. While it is native to Texas and Mexico, it is technically non-native to Florida but behaves perfectly in the landscape without escaping or disrupting local ecosystems.

The "Olive" Confusion: Clarifying that it is in the Boraginaceae family (Borage/Forget-me-not family) and completely unrelated to true olives (Olea europaea) is an excellent, high-value academic point that prevents confusion.

Cold Hardiness: Noting that it is significantly more cold-hardy than the Orange Geiger (Cordia sebestena) is highly accurate and a massive practical selling point for landscapes in Manatee County, where winter cold snaps can occasionally bite the more tropical Geiger.

✂️ Redunda
events.summary: Four targeted edits eliminate the three identified redundancy loops (Geiger/sandpaper, jelly/toxicity, intoxication phrasing) and add the Boraginaceae family note as a high-value academic point. All other fields are untouched.
